name: Grand Duchy of Hesse
alt: Grand Duchy of Hesse and by Rhine

predecessors.name: Landgraviate of Hesse-Darmstadt
predecessors.text: the Landgraviate of Hesse-Darmstadt elevated on 13 August 1806 by joining the Confederation of the Rhine

successors.name: Weimar Republic
successors.text: the state as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918 (People's State of Hesse)

ledger.x: 13 August 1806: Louis I of Hesse-Darmstadt becomes Grand Duke.
1806: Hesse-Homburg is mediatised into the new grand duchy.
24 April 1809: the Teutonic Order lands are merged.
1815: the Congress of Vienna frees Hesse-Homburg.
1815: the Duchy of Westphalia goes to Prussia.
1816: the state takes the name 'Grand Duchy of Hesse and by Rhine'.
1816: Rhenish Hesse joins the grand duchy.
3 September 1866: Hesse loses Biedenkopf, the Hinterland and Hesse-Homburg to Prussia.
3 September 1866: Amt Dorheim is given to the grand duchy.
9 November 1918: the grand duke is removed.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Hesse, on Austria's side, lost the Battle of Frohnhofen near Aschaffenburg (13 July 1866) and the Battle of Tauberbischofsheim (24 July); Prussian troops occupied Darmstadt on 31 July.

wars.name: Franco-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Hesse joined the North German Confederation on 20 October 1870 during the war; no territory changed.

certainty.note: The Napoleonic grand duchy was assembled from the Final Recess lands of 1803 and the 1806 mediatisations; the page names no boundaries and Westphalia was a detached exclave.
Boundaries from the treaty of 30 June 1816 (Rhenish Hesse) and from the treaty of 3 September 1866 (Biedenkopf, the Hinterland, Hesse-Homburg).
